conviction_note: Nothing decisive and unpriced turned up. The H1 FY27 interim (07:00 GMT 17 Nov) brings Q2 Vodafone Spain KPIs the market has not seen, so abs_move is set above the name's 3.4% proxy, at 5.5. The counterparty proxies roughly cancel: Telefonica Espana +2.6% revenue with a raised guide, Orange Espana retail services -1.3%, Vodafone portability still negative but better year on year. A tough Q2 FY26 EBITDAaL comparison and a record of selling results days (4 of 5 down) pull p_up a little under 50, to 47. Findings sum to -0.3 and the scaled number is -0.33; the two agree that there is no edge here.

already_public.what: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026) KPIs: revenue EUR916m (+2% yoy), EBITDA EUR465m (+5%), EBITDAaL EUR324m (+3%), OpCF EUR204m, net debt EUR3.2bn, leverage 2.33x; refinancing closed 14 Jul, run-rate cost of debt c.EUR170m
Capital allocation framework: EUR200m ordinary dividend for FY27 (paid as a final), new EUR200m buyback, leverage target 2.25-2.75x, aim to return all FCF; leverage 2.3x at 30 Jun 2026
Transfer to the ESCC listing category effective 25 Nov 2026, with FTSE UK index eligibility expected at the 22 Mar 2027 rebalance
Interim results date notice: Consolidated Interim Financial Report for the six months to 30 Sep 2026, published 17 Nov 2026 at 07:00 GMT. It contains no numbers

new_in_release.expect: Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep) revenue, EBITDAaL, OpCF and line KPIs have not been seen. Expect low-single-digit revenue growth like Q1 (+2%). The yoy EBITDAaL comparison is against a seasonally high Q2 FY26 EUR349m, so the reported growth could look weaker than Q1's +3%. Direction unknown, slight negative tilt.
H1 OpCF and Holdco net debt and leverage after the buyback started on 24 Sep. Expect leverage near the low end of 2.25-2.75x, as guided. Probably neutral.

Zegona gives no numeric revenue or EBITDA guide in the RNS record I could read, so a guidance change is unlikely. Any FY27 outlook language or a firmer capital-return path is the upside tail. Unknown.
The FY27 EUR200m ordinary dividend is already declared in intent and paid as a final, so no interim dividend is expected. Neutral.
Possible commentary on the reported Telefonica approach and on the RANco mobile-network JV talks with MasOrange. Either sign; probably 'no comment'.

findings.finding: Telefonica Espana, Vodafone Spain's largest rival, reported Q3 2026 revenue of EUR3,316m (+2.6%) and adjusted EBITDA of EUR1,199m (+2.6%), with churn at record lows. The group raised its 2026 EBITDA, OpCFaL and FCF targets, so the Spanish market priced healthily through Vodafone's Q2 (Jul-Sep).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On its last two KPI prints ZEG fell: -4.0% on Q1 FY27 (+2% revenue, 15 Jul 2026) and -6.3% on FY26 (16 Jun 2026). Even solid growth has been sold.
findings.original_quote: Telefónica España ha consolidado su crecimiento con unos ingresos trimestrales de 3.316 millones de euros (+2,6%) y un EBITDA ajustado de 1.199 millones de euros (+2,6%). (Telefonica Espana consolidated its growth with quarterly revenue of EUR3,316m (+2.6%) and adjusted EBITDA of EUR1,199m (+2.6%).)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It was public on 12 Nov and ZEG moved -0.23% that day. It is also partly a share-gain story at Vodafone's expense: Telefonica +180k net portability Jan-Sep. The read-through is the market price level, not Vodafone's volumes, so it is a proxy and sized small.
findings.independence: Same direction for market pricing: Orange Espana's group commentary notes sequential improvement in services (https://roams.es/actualidad/telefonia/orange-espana-ingresa-5673-septiembre-2-mas-gracias-venta-dispositivos/), though its level is negative (finding 2).

findings.finding: Orange Espana (ex-MasOrange), the other incumbent challenger, said its Q3 2026 retail service revenue fell 1.3% yoy to EUR1,368m. Total revenue grew 3.5% only on device sales (+28%) and wholesale, a sign of soft service revenue for the share-losing operators Vodafone sits beside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no direct history on a peer read-through. ZEG's KPI prints have been sold (-4.0%, -6.3%, -5.95% on the 26 Feb 2026 Q3 FY26 report).
findings.original_quote: En el tercer trimestre fueron 1.368 millones, un 1,3% menos, y el comunicado del grupo Orange señala que la tendencia mejora respecto al trimestre anterior. (In Q3 retail services were EUR1,368m, down 1.3%, and Orange's release says the trend improved on the previous quarter.)
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 27 Oct and a peer proxy, so mostly priced. It is filed because, on portability, Orange is the closest structural analogue to Vodafone Spain, and it cuts against the Telefonica read. The sequential-improvement caveat shrinks it.
findings.independence: Portability data showing MasOrange and Vodafone both still losing lines (https://roams.es/actualidad/telefonia/telefonica-gana-clientes-septiembre-digi-masorange-pierde-450000-2026/).

findings.finding: Industry portability data for Jan-Sep 2026 put Vodafone at -110k net mobile ports, better than -135k a year earlier. That excludes Finetwork, which Vodafone bought in late 2025 and which lost more than 100k ports, so the combined group's mobile line trend through Q2 is still negative on switching.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 printed mobile lines +345k yoy (including Finetwork and prepay) and the stock still fell 4.0%. Line KPIs have not driven positive reactions.
findings.original_quote: Vodafone pierde 110.000 frente a los 135.000 del mismo periodo del año anterior ... Estos datos no incluyen a Finetwork, que Vodafone adquirió a finales de 2025 y que acumula una caída de más de 100.000 clientes en portabilidad. (Vodafone loses 110,000 against 135,000 in the same period a year earlier ... These figures exclude Finetwork, acquired by Vodafone at the end of 2025, which has lost more than 100,000 customers on portability.)
findings.why_not_priced: Operator-sourced portability circulates in Spanish trade press and is unlikely to be read closely by the London holder base, but it is a proxy. Reported line KPIs include prepay, IoT and organic gross adds that portability does not capture, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The CNMC July 2026 note says Vodafone's net portability was negative (https://cnmc.es/sites/default/files/editor_contenidos/Notas%20de%20prensa/2026/20260923_NP_Mensual%20telecos%20julio%202026.pdf), and Finetwork brand litigation with Wewi Mobile continues (https://dplnews.com/espana-wewi-mobile-incumple-el-plazo-para-devolver-la-marca-finetwork-a-vodafone/).

findings.finding: The yoy comparison for Q2 is the hardest of the year. Zegona's own disclosures show Vodafone Spain EBITDAaL of EUR349m for the three months to Sept 2025, against EUR316m in Q1 FY26 and EUR313m in Q3 FY26. Repeating Q1 FY27's EUR324m run-rate plus seasonality could print flat-to-low growth against Q1's +3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ZEG fell 4.0% on Q1 FY27, when EBITDAaL growth was +3% and EBITDA +5%. Decelerating profit growth has not been rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts who model the quarter will have the seasonality, so this matters mainly for the headline yoy figure retail and quant readers see. The definitions may not be identical (the Q3 FY26 table excluded Finetwork; Q1 FY27 includes it), which caps it small. It is an inference from primary documents, not a known miss.
findings.independence: Q1 FY26 316 and Q1 FY27 324 come from a separate RNS (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/zegona-communications--zeg/fy27-quarter-1-results/9668915). The independence is weak because both are the company's own figures.

findings.finding: Spanish press reported in September that Telefonica had reactivated talks to buy Vodafone Espana from Zegona. No formal offer has been made, and the two sides' valuations sit about EUR7bn apart (about EUR8bn against about EUR15bn). The interim or its call may carry the first management comment since then.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 14 Sep 2026 report had no clear single-day effect I could isolate. The stock ran from 1672p (27 Oct) to 1886p (4 Nov) and gave it back by 6 Nov with no RNS. Cause unexplained, worth 0.
findings.original_quote: ambas compañías confirman que no se ha presentado ninguna oferta formal para que la operadora dirigida por Marc Murtra compre el negocio de Zegona (both companies confirm that no formal offer has been made for Murtra's operator to buy Zegona's business)
findings.why_not_priced: The talks are public and the stock carries some optionality for them. No offer period exists (no Rule 2.4), so what the window can deliver is commentary of either sign. A 'not for sale at this price' line is as likely as an 'open to value-maximising options' line, so it is sized 0 with a wide band.
findings.independence: Roams (16 Sep 2026) repeats the reactivation and the price gap (https://roams.es/actualidad/telefonia/telefonica-reactiva-compra-vodafone-zegona-vale-mucho-mas/), but it rests on the same reporting.

findings.finding: The EUR200m buyback is running at 40-50k shares a day through Canaccord (240k shares, 9-13 Nov, VWAP 1,750.66p), about 10% of daily volume, and continues mechanically on results day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The day the buyback and dividend framework was announced (24 Sep 2026), ZEG fell 3.2%. Capital returns have been sold as news.
findings.why_not_priced: Fully public and weekly disclosed. It is filed only as a small, dated flow cushion on the day, not as information.
findings.independence: The programme terms are in the 24 Sep RNS (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/zegona-communications--zeg/new-capital-allocation-framework/9787930).

outside_window.finding: Transfer to the ESCC listing category, effective 08:00 on 25 Nov 2026, making ZEG eligible for the FTSE UK Index Series (Travers Smith frames it as facilitating FTSE 250 inclusion), with the rebalance effective 22 Mar 2027. Passive demand lands after the exit window.

Vodafone Espana and MasOrange resumed preliminary talks on a mobile RAN JV (RANco) that could let Zegona monetise a stake, as it did with the fibre JVs (EUR1.8bn). No dated decision inside the window.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is mildly positive (+0.45, mostly a small short and a flat run-up). The findings net slightly negative, and the name's results-day record is negative (4 of 5 down), so the evidence leans weakly against the lean. Nothing is strong enough to beat it, hence p_up 47 rather than lower.
language_note: Spanish trade and financial press (Roams, Vozpopuli, DPL News relaying Expansion) carried the operator portability tallies, including that Finetwork's 100k+ port losses sit outside Vodafone's headline -110k, which no English source I found reports
Spanish press carried the reactivated Telefonica-Zegona talks (14 Sep 2026) and the EUR8bn vs EUR15bn valuation gap. English search returned only 2023-24 deal coverage

The UK domestic RNS record (Investegate) gave the session, the Q2 FY26 EUR349m EBITDAaL comparison base and the buyback run-rate. English wire and sell-side sources added nothing beyond stale price targets
lessons_applied: 'Too small about the move' and 'size on what is new': Q2 FY27 numbers are not pre-released (European base about 7%), but no guidance change is likely and the name's results-day moves cluster at 4-6%, so abs_move_pct went from 4.5 to 5.5. Findings were unchanged
'A finding about a number already told is worth 0': no finding restates the Q1 or capital-allocation numbers; the CAF and ESCC facts are in already_public or outside_window. No change
'In a live bid, results are noise': ZEG is not in an offer period (no Rule 2.4 RNS), so the Telefonica talks stay a 0-sized commentary finding rather than becoming the finding. No change

'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series' and 'a verified fact is not a predicted reaction': the peer and portability proxies were already sized small and p_up already sat near 50 for the sell-the-news history. No further change, to avoid applying the lesson twice
